summary: This is a clipped Snowflake documentation page for the generic CREATE command, which creates a new object of a specified type. It gives the basic syntax (CREATE [OR REPLACE] <object_type> [IF NOT EXISTS] <object_name> with optional type-specific properties, params, and a COMMENT) and two general usage notes: OR REPLACE and IF NOT EXISTS are mutually exclusive, and CREATE OR REPLACE is atomic. The lists of linked object-specific pages (account, database, and class objects) were lost in the clipping, so only the general syntax and notes are usable.
one_line: Snowflake reference page for the generic CREATE command, covering its syntax and general usage notes for creating objects.
key_facts: The CREATE command creates a new object of the specified type.
The basic syntax is CREATE [ OR REPLACE ] <object_type> [ IF NOT EXISTS ] <object_name>, followed by optional object_type_properties, object_type_params, and COMMENT = '<string_literal>'.
The object_type_properties and object_type_params placeholders are specific to each object type.
The OR REPLACE and IF NOT EXISTS clauses are mutually exclusive and cannot both be used in the same statement.
CREATE OR REPLACE statements are atomic: when an object is replaced, the old object is deleted and the new object is created in a single transaction.
The page points readers to object-specific syntax pages for account objects, database objects, and classes.
Class examples named on the page include CREATE CUSTOM_CLASSIFIER and CREATE SNOWFLAKE.ML.ANOMALY_DETECTION.
The page has a 'Was this page helpful?' feedback prompt, and its language is English.
